import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from confkit import ParseError, load, loads


class ExtraTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def err(self, text, **kw):
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            loads(text, **kw)
        return ctx.exception

    def test_scalars(self):
        got = loads("a = 00.5\nb = 1_0.2\nc = -0b101\nd = 1e\ne = 5.\nf = TRUE\ng = 007\nh = inf\n")
        self.assertEqual(got, {"a": 0.5, "b": 10.2, "c": -5, "d": "1e", "e": 5.0,
                               "f": True, "g": "007", "h": "inf"})

    def test_line_endings_and_bom(self):
        self.assertEqual(loads("﻿a = 1\r\nb = 2\rc = 3\n"), {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3})

    def test_list_errors(self):
        for text in ("a = [1,,2]", "a = [,]", "a = [1 2\n", "a = [1]]", "a = [1] x"):
            self.assertTrue(self.err(text).message.startswith("invalid list"), text)
        self.assertTrue(self.err("a = [1,\n 2").message.startswith("unterminated list"))
        self.assertEqual(self.err("a = [1,\n 2").lineno, 1)

    def test_conflicts(self):
        self.assertEqual(loads("[a.b]\n[a]\n"), {"a": {"b": {}}})
        self.assertTrue(self.err("a = 1\na.b = 2").message.startswith("key conflict"))
        self.assertTrue(self.err("a.b = 1\na = 2").message.startswith("key conflict"))
        self.assertTrue(self.err("a = 1\n[a]").message.startswith("key conflict"))

    def test_continuation_errors(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.err("[a]\n  x\n").lineno, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.err("a = 1\n\n  # c\n  2\nb = 1\n  3\n[s]\n x").lineno, 8)

    def test_includes(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            os.mkdir(os.path.join(tmp, "sub"))
            with open(os.path.join(tmp, "sub", "i.ini"), "w") as f:
                f.write("x = 1\n[inner]\ny = 2\n")
            with open(os.path.join(tmp, "m.ini"), "w") as f:
                f.write("[s]\n@include 'sub/i.ini' # c\nz = 3\n")
            self.assertEqual(load(os.path.join(tmp, "m.ini")),
                             {"s": {"x": 1, "inner": {"y": 2}, "z": 3}} if False else
                             {"x": 1, "inner": {"y": 2}, "s": {"z": 3}})
            with open(os.path.join(tmp, "d.ini"), "w") as f:
                f.write('@include "sub/i.ini"\n@include "sub/i.ini"\n')
            with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                load(os.path.join(tmp, "d.ini"))
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.source, os.path.join(tmp, "sub", "i.ini"))
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.lineno, 1)
            self.assertTrue(self.err('@include "q"', base_dir=tmp).message.startswith("cannot read include"))
            self.assertTrue(self.err('@include "q"').message.startswith("include needs"))
            self.assertTrue(self.err('@include q', base_dir=tmp).message.startswith("invalid include"))

    def test_missing_file_is_oserror(self):
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            load("/nonexistent/zzz.ini")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
